html:
Operation Flood was India's national dairy programme, launched in 1970, which turned a milk short country into the world's largest milk producer. It was also called the White Revolution.

It copied the model of Amul, the farmers' cooperative of Anand in Gujarat: village societies collect milk from small farmers twice a day, pay them fairly and fast, and own the dairies that process it. Verghese Kurien, who built Amul, led the National Dairy Development Board, set up in 1965 at the request of Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri.

The first phase was paid for by selling milk powder and butter oil donated by the European Economic Community, later with World Bank loans. A national milk grid linked rural milksheds to the big cities. Over three phases to 1996 it reached tens of thousands of villages, doubled the milk available per person, and in 1998 India passed the United States in output. It ran alongside the Green Revolution in grain.
sum: Operation Flood was India's national dairy programme, launched in 1970, which turned a milk short country into the world's largest milk producer. It was also called the White Revolution.
